stem.en: Most plant and animal cells are 10 to 100 µm across. Your eye can separate points about 0.1 mm apart. Why can you not see most cells without a microscope?

text.en: Cells have no colour, and nothing without colour can be seen at any size.

feedback.en: Stains help us to see cells, but a colourless thing can still be seen if it is large enough.

text.en: Cells move too quickly for the eye to follow them.

feedback.en: Most cells in a tissue stay in place. Speed is not the limit.

text.en: 0.1 mm is 100 µm, so most cells are below that limit.
0.1 mm is 1 µm, so all cells are far above that limit.

feedback.en: Check the conversion. 1 mm is 1000 µm, so 0.1 mm is 100 µm. Being above a limit would also make cells easy to see.

explanation.en:
**Why "0.1 mm is 100 µm" is right**

1 mm = 1000 µm, so 0.1 mm = 100 µm. Most cells are 10 to 100 µm across, which is at or below the limit of the eye.

**Why the others are not**

- **No colour** - size sets the limit here, though stains do help under a microscope.
- **Too quick** - most cells do not race about.
- **0.1 mm is 1 µm** - this conversion is wrong by a factor of 100.
